subject: Hosted API: questions on deletion, backups, and regional purging
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-10T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Qs: Hosted API deletion & backup policy

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — NovaMed's security team had a couple of follow-ups for the hosted API section on data deletion and backups. Can you confirm the following in plain terms?

1) If we ask Redwood to 'delete customer data' for our tenant, what is the expected timeline for:
   - removal from live storage (S3/DBs)
   - removal from short-term caches (KV caches, in-memory)
   - removal from backups / snapshots

2) Are backups geo-replicated? If so, can they be scoped to avoid EU->US replication?

3) What default retention windows do you apply to request logs, token-level traces, and aggregated metrics?

We need concise statements for our security questionnaire and an attachment with a retention diagram if available.

Best,
Elena
Security Analyst, NovaMed
security@novamed.com

--
Note: attaching the questionnaire PDF in a follow-up if helpful.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-10T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: Hosted API deletion & backup policy

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answering inline below; attaching a short retention matrix and a draft M.A.P. (mutual action plan) for NovaMed's security review.

1) Deletion request (tenant-scoped hosted API):
   - Live storage: For customer-configured persistent artifacts (e.g., saved prompts, fine-tune datasets, exported evaluations), Redwood initiates asynchronous deletion within 2 business days and completes sweep of live object stores within 72 hours after initiation.
   - Short-term caches (KV caches, in-memory): KV/prefix caches are evicted immediately on request; any in-memory caches are invalidated within seconds and are not persisted beyond process lifetime.
   - Backups / snapshots: Backups are used for disaster recovery and are retained for the configured recovery window (default 45 days). On deletion request we schedule a forensic purge of snapshots that contain the tenant's objects; purge requests are completed within 30 calendar days by our backup ops process. We provide a certificate of deletion when purge completes.

2) Backup replication & geo-scope:
   - By default, backups are stored in the same cloud region(s) where the tenant's resources live and may be geo-replicated for DR. For NovaMed we can offer region-restriction: configure backups to remain only in EU regions (or US regions) and disable cross-region replication as part of Dedicated/Private or via an enterprise hosted contract. We'll note this in the MAP.

3) Default retention windows (hosted API):
   - Request payloads (customer content): Not persisted by default for hosted API inference requests unless the customer opts-in to store them for features (e.g., prompt history, evals). For tenants with opt-in storage, default retention is 90 days unless otherwise configured.
   - Request metadata / billing logs: 365 days (used for billing, fraud detection, and support).
   - Token-level traces / debug logs: We retain detailed traces for 30 days by default; these are redaction-friendly and can be disabled or shortened on a per-tenant basis.
   - Aggregated metrics / telemetry: 2 years by default; can be exported to your monitoring stack on request.

I've kept the above conservative; Ben and Jonas are cc'd to add technical specifics around snapshot mechanics and encryption. If you want different retention defaults we can surface contract language/options.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Security Lead (Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-hostedapi-retention-matrix.pdf, nova_med_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: Hosted API deletion & backup policy

Thanks — this is helpful. Two clarifications from our control owners: 

A) You mention a 30-day completion for backup purge. Can you clarify whether that is calendar days from request or from the time a snapshot is first identified? NovaMed's policy requires that deletion requests be fully enforced within 30 calendar days of the request submission.

B) For token-level traces: are they tied to tenant IDs? We need to ensure NovaMed tokens are not included in aggregated traces of other tenants used for model debugging.

If convenient, can Ben or Jonas provide the short statement we can drop into our questionnaire under the question "Are customer data removed from backups within 30 days of request?"

Best,
Elena

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2029-10-10T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs: Hosted API deletion & backup policy

Elena — quick technical note to confirm and provide the exact phrasing you can paste into the questionnaire: 

"Upon receipt of a tenant-initiated data deletion request, Redwood Inference schedules a removal of the tenant's objects from live stores within 72 hours and initiates a backup/snapshot purge workflow. Backups are purged within 30 calendar days from the date of the customer's deletion request; customers receive confirmation when purge completes. For tenants with region-restriction enabled, backups are constrained to the configured region and are not replicated outside that region unless explicitly requested in the contract."

Additional answers:
- Token-level traces are recorded under tenant-scoped trace IDs and are accessible only to engineers and reviewers with tenant-level access. Traces used for cross-tenant model debugging are aggregated and do not include tenant identifiers or raw customer tokens.
- All backups and snapshots are encrypted at-rest with customer-data encryption keys (managed by Redwood's KMS) and are logged to an auditable deletion queue for compliance.

Let me know if you want the wording tightened further; we can also provide an ops playbook snippet for inclusion in your RFP pack.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment note: retention matrix shows default and optional windows and a checkbox for region-only backup enforcement.
